overview.body: This is a MASTER unit: the finished Module 3 game! Hazards come from parallel lists, the report counts your cities and scores your escapes, and every finished game writes a trip report you can open after the game closes. Lab 4.1 starts from exactly what you finish here.

mentorQuote.quote: A road trip isn't over when you park. It's over when you tell someone about it. The trip report is the game telling the story for you, and it's still there tomorrow.

objectives: Keep the hazards in three parallel lists, picked by one library function
Build a list of unique cities with not in and append()
Show an escape rate with one decimal place, and never divide by zero
Write a formatted trip report file, building the route line in a loop
Handle a save file that puts you at a beach

testingPins.intro: A pin swaps a random line for a fixed value, so a test comes out the same every time. Comment out the line in the second column and put the line from the third column right under it, at the same indent. When a test needs a different value (like roll = 5), it says so. To restore a pin, delete the fixed line and take the # off the original. A pin stays in your file until a step changes it or says to restore it, so pins from earlier checkpoints may still be there. A pin a test doesn't mention can stay as it is: with the roll at 20, every leg takes one turn and the hazard lines never run. A value in parentheses in the last column is the one that checkpoint uses.
testingPins.restore: Every pin MUST be restored before you submit: CodeGrade runs the random lines itself, with its own fixed numbers.

# ============================================================
# HAZARD HELPER (Added in Lab 3-3)
# ============================================================

def get_random_hazard(names, heads_msgs, tails_msgs):
    """
    Pick a random hazard from three parallel lists.

    Args:
        names (list): The hazards
        heads_msgs (list): What happens on HEADS, in the same order
        tails_msgs (list): What happens on TAILS, in the same order

    Returns:
        tuple: A hazard and its HEADS and TAILS messages
    """
    index = random.randint(0, len(names) - 1)
    return names[index], heads_msgs[index], tails_msgs[index]

content.body: Two new numbers in the report: how many different cities you visited, and what percent of your hazards you escaped.

A trip home from Austin puts San Antonio on the route twice. To count each city once, build a second list: go through the route, and append() a city only when it's not in the new list yet. The escape rate divides escapes by hazards, so it only makes sense when there was at least one hazard; dividing by zero stops the program. f'{escape_rate:.1f}' turns the number into a string with one digit after the decimal point.

content.quote: Raw totals are fine. A percentage is a score. Players will replay a trip just to push their escape rate up, and 'four cities' sounds like a road trip in a way that 'five stops' doesn't.

content.body: A trip report that outlives the game. After every finished game, the report goes into trip_report.txt, in its own plain layout: the route on one line with arrows, the statistics, and the hazards A to Z.

Lab 3.1 wrote a file for the program to read back; this one is for people to read. The function opens the file in 'w' mode, so each game's report replaces the last one. Its layout is simpler than the screen's, so it builds the route as one line: start with an empty string and add each city, with ' -> ' before every city but the first. The hazards need to be sorted before the screen report now, because the file uses them too.

content.quote: I check the file, not just the screen. Open trip_report.txt after every run: forty equals signs, the arrows, two spaces in front of the statistics. If the file is off by one character, it's off.

items: Under HAZARD_CHANCE, name the file:
Above def main():, with two empty lines above and below, add the function:

content.code:
def save_trip_report(filename, player_name, current_city, total_miles,
                     total_turns, total_hazards, total_escaped,
                     visited_cities, unique_cities, sorted_hazards,
                     status):
    """
    Write the trip report to a file.

    Args:
        filename (str): The file to write
        player_name (str): The player's name
        current_city (str): Where the game ended
        total_miles (int): Miles this game
        total_turns (int): Turns this game
        total_hazards (int): Hazards faced this game
        total_escaped (int): Hazards escaped this game
        visited_cities (list): Every city this game, in order
        unique_cities (list): Each city once
        sorted_hazards (list): The hazards, A to Z
        status (str): How the game ended
    """
    outfile = open(filename, 'w')

    outfile.write('DEEP IN THE HEART - TRIP REPORT\n')
    outfile.write('=' * 40 + '\n')
    outfile.write(f'Driver: {player_name}\n')
    outfile.write(f'Final City: {current_city}\n')
    outfile.write(f'Status: {status}\n')
    outfile.write('\n')

    outfile.write('ROUTE:\n')
    route_str = ''
    for city in visited_cities:
        if route_str != '':
            route_str = route_str + ' -> '
        route_str = route_str + city
    outfile.write(f'  {route_str}\n')
    outfile.write(f'  Unique cities visited: {len(unique_cities)}\n')

    outfile.write(f'  Hazards Faced: {total_hazards}\n')
    outfile.write(f'  Hazards Escaped: {total_escaped}\n')
    if total_hazards > 0:
        rate = (total_escaped / total_hazards) * 100
        rate_str = f'{rate:.1f}'
        outfile.write(f'  Escape Rate: {rate_str}%\n')
    outfile.write('\n')

    outfile.write('HAZARDS (A-Z):\n')
    if len(sorted_hazards) > 0:
        for hazard in sorted_hazards:
            outfile.write('  - ' + hazard + '\n')
    else:
        outfile.write('  None - Lucky traveler!\n')
    outfile.write('\n')

    outfile.write('=' * 40 + '\n')
    outfile.close()
